blocks.text: The C-X bond in halogenoalkanes is polar due to the difference of electronegativity between C and the halogen atom. The carbon of C-X acts as an electrophilic centre, which can be attacked by a nucleophile. Alternatively, the hydrogen attached to the carbon atom may be attacked by a base. These two possibilities result in two types of reaction of halogenoalkanes
a) Those reactions in which the halogen is replaced by some other atom or a group (nucleophilic substitution, or SN reactions),

blocks.alt: Nu- with a curly arrow to the delta+ carbon of a substrate C-X (delta- on X), and a curly arrow from the C-X bond to X. The arrow gives Nu-C, with the other three bonds now on the opposite side, + X-. Labels: Attacking Nucleophile, Substrate Molecule, Substituted Product, Leaving Group.
blocks.caption: Nucleophilic substitution reaction (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 79).

blocks.text: b) Those that involve the removal of HX from halogenoalkanes (elimination, or E reactions), results in the formation of alkenes.

blocks.alt: A substrate with two bonded carbons, H on one and X on the next (both in a dashed box), gives an alkene C=C + HX. Labels: Substrate Molecule, Alkene, Hydrogen Halide.
blocks.caption: Elimination reaction (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 79).
